passages.text: A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
This is a prayer.
A person prays this prayer.
This person feels afflicted.
This person grows faint.
This person pours out his lament.
He pours out his lament before the LORD.

passages.text: Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry for help come before You.
passages.sermon:
A poor and afflicted person prays.
He feels weak and overwhelmed.
He pours out his complaint before the LORD.
He speaks honestly to God.
He says, “LORD, hear my prayer.”
He asks God to listen to his cry for help.
He wants his plea to come before God.
passages.original: תְּ֭פִלָּה לְעָנִ֣י כִֽי־ יַעֲטֹ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ שִׂיחֽוֹ׃ יְ֭הוָה שִׁמְעָ֣ה תְפִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝שַׁוְעָתִ֗י אֵלֶ֥יךָ תָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Do not hide Your face from me in my day of distress. Incline Your ear to me; answer me quickly when I call.
passages.sermon:
A person suffers.
He feels weak and troubled.
He prays to the LORD.
He says, “LORD, do not turn away from me when I am in trouble.
Listen to me.
When I call to You, answer me quickly.”
passages.original: אַל־ תַּסְתֵּ֬ר פָּנֶ֨יךָ׀ מִמֶּנִּי֮ בְּי֪וֹם צַ֫ר לִ֥י הַטֵּֽה־ אֵלַ֥י אָזְנֶ֑ךָ בְּי֥וֹם אֶ֝קְרָ֗א מַהֵ֥ר עֲנֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: For my days vanish like smoke, and my bones burn like glowing embers.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a poor and afflicted person.
The speaker prays to the LORD.
The speaker says, "My days disappear quickly."
My days vanish like smoke.
My bones feel hot and burned.
My bones burn like glowing embers.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ כָל֣וּ בְעָשָׁ֣ן יָמָ֑י וְ֝עַצְמוֹתַ֗י כְּמוֹ־ קֵ֥ד נִחָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: My heart is afflicted, and withered like grass; I even forget to eat my bread.
passages.sermon: The speaker feels deep sorrow in his heart.\r\nHis heart is weak and dried up like grass.\r\nHe is so troubled that he forgets to eat his bread.
passages.original: הוּכָּֽה־ כָ֭עֵשֶׂב וַיִּבַ֣שׁ לִבִּ֑י כִּֽי־ שָׁ֝כַ֗חְתִּי מֵאֲכֹ֥ל לַחְמִֽי׃

passages.text: Through my loud groaning my flesh clings to my bones.
passages.sermon:
The speaker suffers deeply.
The speaker groans loudly.
The speaker’s pain is intense.
The speaker’s body grows thin.
The speaker’s flesh sticks to his bones.
passages.original: מִקּ֥וֹל אַנְחָתִ֑י דָּבְקָ֥ה עַ֝צְמִ֗י לִבְשָׂרִֽי׃

passages.text: I am like a desert owl, like an owl among the ruins.
passages.sermon:
The speaker feels alone.
The speaker compares himself to a desert owl.
A desert owl lives in empty, dry places.
The speaker also feels like an owl among ruins.
An owl among ruins sits in broken, abandoned places.
The speaker feels isolated and abandoned.
passages.original: דָּ֭מִיתִי לִקְאַ֣ת מִדְבָּ֑ר הָ֝יִ֗יתִי כְּכ֣וֹס חֳרָבֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I lie awake; I am like a lone bird on a housetop.
passages.sermon:
The speaker cannot sleep.
The speaker stays awake at night.
The speaker feels alone.
The speaker is like a bird.
The bird sits alone on a rooftop.
passages.original: שָׁקַ֥דְתִּי וָאֶֽהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝צִפּ֗וֹר בּוֹדֵ֥ד עַל־ גָּֽג׃

passages.text: All day long my enemies taunt me; they ridicule me and curse me.
passages.sermon:
My enemies taunt me all day long.
They ridicule me.
They curse me.
They do this constantly.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַ֭יּוֹם חֵרְפ֣וּנִי אוֹיְבָ֑י מְ֝הוֹלָלַ֗י בִּ֣י נִשְׁבָּֽעוּ׃

passages.text: For I have eaten ashes like bread and mixed my drink with tears because of Your indignation and wrath, for You have picked me up and cast me aside.
passages.sermon:
The speaker suffers deeply.
The speaker eats ashes as if they were bread.
The speaker mixes his drink with his own tears.
God is angry with the speaker.
God shows indignation and wrath.
God lifts up the speaker.
God throws the speaker aside.
passages.original: כִּי־ אֵ֭פֶר כַּלֶּ֣חֶם אָכָ֑לְתִּי וְ֝שִׁקֻּוַ֗י בִּבְכִ֥י מָסָֽכְתִּי׃ מִפְּנֵֽי־ זַֽעַמְךָ֥ וְקִצְפֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י נְ֝שָׂאתַ֗נִי וַתַּשְׁלִיכֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: My days are like lengthening shadows, and I wither away like grass.
passages.sermon: The speaker describes himself.\r\nHe says his days are like shadows that grow longer.\r\nHe says he is like grass that dries up and withers.
passages.original: יָ֭מַי כְּצֵ֣ל נָט֑וּי וַ֝אֲנִ֗י כָּעֵ֥שֶׂב אִיבָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: But You, O LORD, sit enthroned forever; Your renown endures to all generations.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD sits on His throne forever.
The LORD never leaves His throne.
People remember the LORD in every generation.
The LORD’s name lasts for all time.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֑ב וְ֝זִכְרְךָ֗ לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃

passages.text: You will rise up and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to show her favor— the appointed time has come.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is eternal.
The LORD rules forever.
The LORD will act.
The LORD will show compassion to Zion.
Now is the time to show favor to Zion.
The appointed time has arrived.
passages.original: אַתָּ֣ה תָ֭קוּם תְּרַחֵ֣ם צִיּ֑וֹן כִּי־ עֵ֥ת לְ֝חֶֽנְנָ֗הּ כִּי־ בָ֥א מוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: For Your servants delight in her stones and take pity on her dust.
passages.sermon:
God has servants.
These servants love Zion.
They find joy in Zion’s stones.
They care about Zion’s dust.
They show compassion to even the smallest parts of Zion.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ רָצ֣וּ עֲ֭בָדֶיךָ אֶת־ אֲבָנֶ֑יהָ וְֽאֶת־ עֲפָרָ֥הּ יְחֹנֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: So the nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth will fear Your glory.
passages.sermon: The nations will fear the name of the LORD.\r\nAll the kings of the earth will fear Your glory.
passages.original: וְיִֽירְא֣וּ ג֭וֹיִם אֶת־ שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־ מַלְכֵ֥י הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ אֶת־ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For the LORD will rebuild Zion; He has appeared in His glory.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD will rebuild Zion.
The LORD has appeared.
The LORD has appeared in His glory.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ בָנָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה צִיּ֑וֹן נִ֝רְאָ֗ה בִּכְבוֹדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He will turn toward the prayer of the destitute; He will not despise their prayer.
passages.sermon: The LORD listens to the prayer of the destitute.\r\nThe LORD does not reject their prayer.
passages.original: פָּ֭נָה אֶל־ תְּפִלַּ֣ת הָעַרְעָ֑ר וְלֹֽא־ בָ֝זָ֗ה אֶת־ תְּפִלָּתָֽם׃

passages.text: Let this be written for the generation to come, so that a people not yet created may praise the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God wants this message written down.
He wants it saved for a future generation.
This generation does not exist yet.
God will create these people.
These people will praise the LORD.
passages.original: תִּכָּ֣תֶב זֹ֭את לְד֣וֹר אַחֲר֑וֹן וְעַ֥ם נִ֝בְרָ֗א יְהַלֶּל־ יָֽהּ׃

passages.text: For He looked down from the heights of His sanctuary; the LORD gazed out from heaven to earth to hear a prisoner’s groaning, to release those condemned to death, that they may proclaim the name of the LORD in Zion and praise Him in Jerusalem, when peoples and kingdoms assemble to serve the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is holy.
He lives in heaven.
He looked down from His high and holy place.
He gazed from heaven to the earth.
He listened for the groaning of prisoners.
He wanted to set free those sentenced to die.
He did this so people would speak His name in Zion.
He did this so people would praise Him in Jerusalem.
Peoples and kingdoms will gather together.
They will serve the LORD.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִ֭שְׁקִיף מִמְּר֣וֹם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ יְ֝הוָ֗ה מִשָּׁמַ֤יִם׀ אֶל־ אֶ֬רֶץ הִבִּֽיט׃ לִ֭שְׁמֹעַ אֶנְקַ֣ת אָסִ֑יר לְ֝פַתֵּ֗חַ בְּנֵ֣י תְמוּתָֽה׃ לְסַפֵּ֣ר בְּ֭צִיּוֹן שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וּ֝תְהִלָּת֗וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ בְּהִקָּבֵ֣ץ עַמִּ֣ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וּ֝מַמְלָכ֗וֹת לַעֲבֹ֥ד אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: He has broken my strength on the way; He has cut short my days.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and authority.
God has broken my strength.
God has done this while I am on my journey.
God has cut short my days.
passages.original: עִנָּ֖ה בַדֶּ֥רֶךְ כֹּחוֹ קִצַּ֥ר יָמָֽי׃

passages.text: I say: “O my God, do not take me in the midst of my days! Your years go on through all generations.
passages.sermon:
I speak to God.
I say, "O my God, do not let me die in the middle of my life."
Your years continue through every generation.
You live forever.
You do not end.
You remain the same in every age.
passages.original: אֹמַ֗ר אֵלִ֗י אַֽל־ תַּ֭עֲלֵנִי בַּחֲצִ֣י יָמָ֑י בְּד֖וֹר דּוֹרִ֣ים שְׁנוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: In the beginning You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
passages.sermon:
God acted in the beginning.
God laid the foundations of the earth.
God made the heavens.
The heavens are the work of God's hands.
passages.original: לְ֭פָנִים הָאָ֣רֶץ יָסַ֑דְתָּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ שָׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing You will change them, and they will be passed on.
passages.sermon:
God created the earth and the heavens.
The earth and the heavens will perish.
God will remain.
The earth and the heavens will wear out like a garment.
God will change them like clothing.
They will pass away.
God will not pass away.
passages.original: הֵ֤מָּה׀ יֹאבֵדוּ֮ וְאַתָּ֪ה תַ֫עֲמֹ֥ד וְ֭כֻלָּם כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֑וּ כַּלְּב֖וּשׁ תַּחֲלִיפֵ֣ם וְֽיַחֲלֹֽפוּ׃

passages.text: But You remain the same, and Your years will never end.
passages.sermon:
God never changes.
God always stays the same.
God’s years never end.
God lives forever.
passages.original: וְאַתָּה־ ה֑וּא וּ֝שְׁנוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א יִתָּֽמּוּ׃

passages.text: The children of Your servants will dwell securely, and their descendants will be established before You.”
passages.sermon:
God is eternal and unchanging.
God’s servants have children.
The children of God’s servants will live in safety.
The descendants of God’s servants will stand firm before God.
God will establish the descendants of His servants.
passages.original: בְּנֵֽי־ עֲבָדֶ֥יךָ יִשְׁכּ֑וֹנוּ וְ֝זַרְעָ֗ם לְפָנֶ֥יךָ יִכּֽוֹן׃
